title: Count Special Integers
summary: Define a special integer as one where all digits are unique.
statement: Define a special integer as one where all digits are unique. Given a positive integer n, count how many special integers exist within the range from 1 to n.
constraints: A positive integer is special when none of its decimal digits repeat.
Return the count of special integers from one through n inclusive.
hints: Process decimal positions while remembering used digits, whether the number has started, and whether the prefix equals n.
A ten-bit mask rejects repeated non-leading digits.
Digit DP tries 0 through the tight limit; leading zeros do not enter the mask; the terminal state counts only started numbers.
Every integer at most n has one padded digit path, tightness enforces the upper bound, and the mask accepts exactly distinct-digit paths.
editorial: Every integer at most n has one padded digit path, tightness enforces the upper bound, and the mask accepts exactly distinct-digit paths.

tests.explanation: Every positive integer through twenty except eleven has distinct digits, giving nineteen.
Digit counting finds 110 special positive integers no greater than 135.
